pr_title: REGR: Assigning label with registered EA dtype raises
pr_body:
- [x] closes #38386
- [x] tests added / passed
- [x] passes `black pandas`
- [x] passes `git diff upstream/master -u -- "*.py" | flake8 --diff`
- [x] whatsnew entry

Previous behavior in `io.parsers` depended on `is_bool_dtype("boolean")` erroneously raising `AttributeError`.

Test currently iterates over the names:

> ['category', 'interval', 'boolean', 'Float32', 'Float64', 'Int8', 'Int16', 'Int32', 'Int64', 'UInt8', 'UInt16', 'UInt32', 'UInt64', 'string']

It skips any EA where the name is a property; I don't see a good way to iterate over these in the test.

I only added a note about `is_bool_dtype` in the whatsnew as the `DataFrame.__setitem__` issue does not occur on 1.1.x. It didn't seem appropriate for any section besides other.

comments:
I suppose this is caused by #38030 (@jbrockmendel)

That PR introduced:

https://github.com/pandas-dev/pandas/blob/3aa84479e54612eb58dd12d2d1f02674acc321c4/pandas/core/indexes/numeric.py#L173-L176

but the problem here is that the validation function is not raising a TypeError, but a different error. This, in turn, seems to be caused by a bug in `is_bool_dtype`:

```
In [36]: pd.api.types.is_bool_dtype("Int64")
```

Agreed we should fix this in is_bool_dtype
